title: feat(metadata-protocol): one language of an email template is addressed by name — the by-name /meta doors accept a bundle member selector (#22877, stage 2)
body:
Fixes #22877
Clause-②: yes
Widens: the accept set of the five by-name `/meta` doors (GET, DELETE, `/history`, `/publish`, `/rollback` on `/meta/:type/:name`) by one query parameter, `member`, and the four protocol requests behind them (`GetMetaItemRequest`, `DeleteMetaItemRequest`, `PublishMetaItemRequest`, `HistoryMetaItemRequest`) by one optional field, `member`; and three exported surfaces, each by one optional `member`: the last argument of `SchemaRegistry.getItem`, `getArtifactItem`, `removeRuntimeShadow` and `removeOverlayEntry` (`@objectstack/objectql`), the `MetadataMutationEvent` field (`@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, also carried on the `ClusterMetadataMutationPayload` a peer accepts), and the header on each `SysMetadataRepository.listDrafts` entry.

Stage 2 of 2 of ruling 6116165299 (letter A, Q2 i). Stage 1 (PR #22954, `5677add93f`) stores two locales of one `email_template` as two `sys_metadata` rows (`bundle_member`); every by-name door was still canonical-only. This PR lets each by-name door address one member, and carries the four items stage 1 left (seat answers 6118224899, landing record 6121513183).

The ruling, quoted:

> **Q2 → i:** `PUT` stays body-addressed. GET, DELETE, publish, history and revert by name accept one member selector in their closed query-parameter set (AGENTS.md route rule 5), named after the discriminator so it cannot be read as the UI translation locale (`?locale=` on `/meta` already means that); absent, it means the canonical member, which is what the registry's bare-name read answers; a wrong value is a located 400. This widens the doors' accept set: `Clause-②: yes`, a contract-tier review before landing.

## What changed

### 1. The selector (`metadata-protocol`, `rest`, `spec`)

- **The name is `member`.** It is what the stored column holds (`sys_metadata.bundle_member`), and it is type-neutral. It is not `locale`, which on `/meta` already names the response translation locale (`extractLocale`). The seat suggested `member`; nothing measured argued for another name.
- **One reading, shared by every door:** `resolveBundleMemberSelector` in `protocol.ts`, beside stage 1's member plumbing. Each of the five protocol doors calls it once, right after its type fold: `getMetaItem`, `deleteMetaItem`, `publishMetaItem`, `historyMetaItem`, `rollbackMetaItem`.
  - Absent means the canonical member. Naming the canonical value (`en-US`) is the same request. The value is trimmed.
  - Refused with a located 400 `VALIDATION_ERROR` (`param: 'member'`, the message names the selector):
    - a selector on a type with no discriminator (every type except `email_template`);
    - a value that is not a string;
    - a blank value (never read as absent);
    - a value longer than 100 characters, the declared `maxLength` of `bundle_member` (pinned equal to `SysMetadataObject`).
  - A well-formed member with nothing stored or shipped, measured per door:
    - GET answers it as absent (protocol `item: undefined`, REST 404);
    - DELETE answers `reset: false`;
    - publish answers `404 NO_DRAFT`;
    - history answers `{ events: [] }`;
    - revert answers `404 VERSION_NOT_FOUND`.
- **The requests carry it.** The REST door builds each typed request literal against the spec request shapes (`TransportScopedMetaRequest`). So `GetMetaItemRequestSchema`, `DeleteMetaItemRequestSchema`, `PublishMetaItemRequestSchema` and `HistoryMetaItemRequestSchema` gain one optional `member` with one shared describe (cross-lane `domain:spec`). `rollbackMetaItem` has no declared request (the door calls it through a cast), so none was added. `authorable-surface/api.json` and `content/docs/references/api/protocol.mdx` are regenerated.

### 2. The five routes' closed query sets (`rest`, AGENTS.md route rule 5)

None of the five routes declared a closed set before. Each set below is measured from the handler's own read points and from the helpers it calls, and each route now opens with `refuseUnknownQueryParams`, ahead of its arity gate:

| route | closed set | read points |
|:---|:---|:---|
| `GET /meta/:type/:name` | `layers`, `state`, `preview`, `package`, `locale`, `member` | `wantsMetaItemLayers`; the two admitted draft switches; `metaItemPackageBinding` and `serveMetaItemLayered`; `locale` a frame down (`extractLocale` behind the cached validator and every translation) |
| `DELETE /meta/:type/:name` | `state`, `dropStorage`, `member` | the draft discard and the opt-in teardown |
| `GET …/history` | `sinceSeq`, `limit`, `member` | the declared paging pair |
| `POST …/publish` | `package`, `member` | `metaItemPackageBinding` |
| `POST …/rollback` | `toVersion`, `member` | the query fallback after the body |

- `member` joins each route's `refuseRepeatedQueryParams` list too.
- One reading of the parameter, `metaMemberSelector`, is shared by the five handlers. It passes a non-string value through, so the protocol refuses it; it is never dropped.
- A GET naming a member bypasses the cached arm, because `getMetaItemCached` takes no member.
- `?layers=` together with `?member=` is refused. The layered view reads no member, and answering with the canonical member's layers would be the silent wrong answer.
- In-repo callers were measured, and none sends a parameter outside these sets: `@objectstack/client` and `objectui` at the pinned `9646e2ed2b` (`DraftChangesPanel`, `ResourceEditPage`, `client.meta.*`).

### 3. The registry's bare-name read (`objectql` `SchemaRegistry.getItem`)

- A bare-name read of a discriminated type now answers the **canonical** member, wherever it sits in the tier order (overlay, then prefer-local, then the first composite).
- Before, the first tier that held any member won, and canonical-first applied only inside that tier. So a `zh-CN`-only overlay answered a read that named no member. This was the half-false premise recorded in 6118224899.
- A bundle with no canonical member still answers its first member, as before.
- `getItem` and `getArtifactItem` take an optional `member` (a discriminator value), which narrows every tier to that member.

### 4. `removeRuntimeShadow` on a by-name reset (stage 1 finding 1)

- `removeRuntimeShadow(type, name, member?)` and `removeOverlayEntry(type, name, member?)` address one member when one is named. With no member, they keep the group sweep, the shape `unregisterItem` takes for a withdrawal by name.
- `restoreArtifactRegistryView` names the member on every tier. A MetadataService baseline of another member is not this member's baseline: that service keys a type's items by name alone.
- **Found by the dogfood, fixed here:** a member's shadow is lifted when the bundle ships *any* artifact, not only an artifact of that member.
  - A hydrated overlay of a member the package does not ship wears the bundle's artifact envelope (`_packageId`, `_provenance` grafted by `mergeArtifactProtection`). So `removeOverlayEntry` refuses it as code.
  - On the showcase, a `zh-CN` reset therefore kept sending the reset wording until the next boot.
  - It is pinned in the objectql harness against a versioned package, so artifacts carry the envelope.

### 5. Package-batch doors and the cluster fan-out (stage 1 finding 2)

- `SysMetadataRepository.listDrafts` headers carry the stored `member` when it is non-canonical. The protocol's public `listDrafts` serves its declared header without it.
- **`publishPackageDrafts`:**
  - each draft is promoted as its member;
  - the pre-publish capture reads that member's active row;
  - the revert plan item records `member`;
  - a failed batch names the causal draft by member.
- **`discardPackageDrafts`** (and `revertStoredPackage`, through `discardDraftInItsScope`) discards each draft as its member.
- **`revertCommit`** reads, deletes, restores, re-binds and heals each plan item as its member. The revert's own plan carries the member too. `listCommits` serves the declared four keys.
- **The cluster fan-out:**
  - `MetadataMutationEvent` gains an optional `member` (present only for a non-canonical member);
  - save, publish, delete, rollback and revert stamp it;
  - `applyRemoteMetadataMutation` re-reads, re-binds and heals that member's row.

## Pins (real code)

`packages/objectql/src/environment-overlay-email-locale-restart.test.ts`, stage 1's harness (real `ObjectQL` and protocol; a restart is a new engine over the same stores). It is now a versioned package that also ships an `en-US`-only template:

- GET: each member by name; absent and `en-US` both answer the canonical member; trimmed.
- GET: a member nobody stored answers the code layer's member; one that no layer holds answers nothing.
- DELETE by member: `zh-CN` reset → its row alone goes, and the `en-US` overlay stays the registry's entry, at once and after a restart.
- DELETE of a member no artifact ships: its overlay leaves the registry and the layered list, and the canonical overlay stays.
- DELETE with no member (the reverse): the canonical member is reset, and the `zh-CN` overlay stays registered.
- publish by member: a `zh-CN` draft goes live. CONTROL: the bare publish answers `NO_DRAFT`.
- history and revert by member:
  - one shared counter, three distinct versions;
  - each member sees its own events;
  - a revert to another member's version answers `404 VERSION_NOT_FOUND`.
- CONTROL: a bare-name revert reverts the canonical member to its own version and leaves `zh-CN`.
- A wrong selector is a located 400 on all five doors (a `view` type, blank, 101 characters), and the store bytes are unchanged.
- `publishPackageDrafts`, `revertCommit` and `discardPackageDrafts` with a two-member bundle where `zh-CN` alone has a draft. The commit timeline and the draft list keep their declared keys.
- The cluster fan-out (two control-plane replicas over one store, a delivering bus): the peer converges on the member that changed, and a member reset heals only that member.
- The six stage 1 pins, unchanged.

`packages/objectql/src/registry-i18n-bundle-key.test.ts`:

- the bare-name read answers the canonical member with a `zh-CN`-only overlay;
- named-member reads, artifact included;
- the member-addressed heal, including the shipped-bundle and unshipped-bundle cases; naming no member keeps the sweep.

`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.bundle-member-selector.test.ts`: the one reading — every refusal, the trimmed pass, and the length bound pinned equal to the declared column.

`packages/rest/src/rest-server-meta-member-selector.test.ts`, 30 cases. Per route:

- **refusal:** a misspelled selector is answered with status, nested `error.code` and the exact located message, and the protocol is never called; a repeated selector is refused;
- **preservation:** the exact request the protocol received, the member and every measured name included, `locale` too; GET bypasses the cache with a member and keeps it without one;
- the layered refusal;
- a CONTROL that no selector sends no `member` key;
- the value refusals from a **real** protocol over an engine that is never reached.

`packages/qa/dogfood/test/email-template-two-locales-survive-boot.dogfood.test.ts`, stage 1's showcase case extended, on a real SQLite file and real `sendTemplate`:

- `?member=zh-CN` reads the `zh-CN` wording;
- `DELETE ?member=zh-CN` resets `zh-CN` alone;
- after a cold boot, `en-US` keeps the admin's wording and `zh-CN` falls to the `en-US` floor (the showcase ships `en-US` only);
- `?member=zh-CN` is then 404;
- a misspelled selector, and a selector on a type with no members, are located 400s.

This case also measures that the showcase's `/meta` item read is served by `RestServer`'s route, which reads the selector.

## Evidence

Every heavy run went through `scripts/pm/os-verify-lock.sh`, and each read its `VERDICT command-exit 0` line. Exit codes were captured before any pipe. The final head is `2b882e6774`, which merges `origin/main` `df7a137923`; the incoming commits touch none of this PR's files.

**Gates.**

- The derived union is `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` at `2b882e6774`: **118 commands, 118 exit 0**.
- Reconciled with `--ran` (exit codes recorded): `118 derived, 118 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN`.
- The lead list of 86 commands at `0ede0f8ab3` is a subset of it.
- An earlier round at `12b4b5047f` had `check:skill-examples` and `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` at exit 3 (PREREQUISITE NOT MET). After a full packages build (`turbo`, 72 tasks, exit 0) both pass, and the final round has them green.

**Suites.**

- `objectql`, full (`vitest run`): `Test Files 407 passed (407)`, `Tests 7955 passed`. This ran before the last registry commit (`2b882e6774`).
- After that commit:
  - every `objectql` test file that names `removeRuntimeShadow`, `removeOverlayEntry` or `email_template`: 13 files, `246 passed`;
  - the restart harness and the registry bundle file: 2 files, `40 passed`.
- `metadata-protocol`, full, at `12b4b5047f`: `Test Files 228 passed | 3 skipped (231)`, `Tests 28196 passed | 19 skipped`.
- `rest`, full, at `00886e17d7` (the merge touched no `rest` file): `Test Files 279 passed (279)`, `Tests 5960 passed | 327 skipped`. After the merge, 6 targeted files (the new pins, the closed-set and multiplicity files, absent-404, history/diff door, publish package scope): `141 passed`.
- `spec`: `protocol.test.ts` and `type-alias-convention.pin.test.ts`, `187 passed`.
- Typecheck exit 0 for `spec`, `metadata-protocol`, `objectql` (with `check:test-typecheck`), `rest` (with `check:test-typecheck`) and `dogfood`.
- `dogfood`: `email-template-two-locales-survive-boot.dogfood.test.ts`, `4 passed (4)`, after `objectql` was rebuilt at `2b882e6774`.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec check:generated` named `check:docs` stale; `gen:docs` regenerated one page. `check:authorable-surface` wrote the 4 new request keys into `authorable-surface/api.json`.

**ESLint, a proven narrowing.**

- `pnpm exec eslint --no-inline-config --format json` over the 11 changed `.ts` files: 11 files linted, 0 errors, 0 warnings.
- The population is `eslint.config.mjs`'s `files: ['**/*.{ts,tsx,mts,cts,js,jsx,mjs,cjs}']` minus `NEVER_LINTED`. No file was reported ignored.
- That config never enables type-aware linting (no `parserOptions.project`, as its own header records), so this diff cannot move the verdict on any file it does not touch.
- The repo-wide `pnpm lint` is CI's.

## Ablations

Each ablation went through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` (wrap mode, on committed HEAD; anchor count 1 then 0, blob changed, restored blob equal to HEAD, `git diff HEAD` empty). A `metadata-protocol` mutation was rebuilt, because `objectql` resolves it through `dist`, a `KNOWN_UNALIASED_TEST_IMPORTS` pair. `ablation-dist-preflight` was run present on the mutation leg and `--absent` on the restore leg.

1. **`rollbackMetaItem` without the member** (the `restoreVersion` member option replaced by an expression that is `undefined` at runtime, with the marker `__ABLATION_22877_ROLLBACK_MEMBER_DROPPED`). The restart harness went `1 failed | 17 passed`. Only the member-revert pin was red (`No history row at version 2 … (its canonical member)`); the bare-name revert CONTROL stayed green. Restored: `18 passed`.
2. **The registry tier-order change** (`getItem`'s bare-name branch back to the first tier's first member, with the marker `__ABLATION_22877_REGISTRY_TIER_ORDER`; `objectql` source, so no build). The registry bundle file and the harness went `1 failed | 38 passed`. Only `a bare-name read answers the canonical member when only a second locale is overlaid` was red. The harness's bare-name pins stay green under this ablation, because `getMetaItem` answers the canonical artifact before it asks the registry, which is a second layer by design. Restored: `39 passed`.
3. **The registry heal without the member** (`removeRuntimeShadow(singular, name, memberKey)` with `memberKey` replaced). The harness went `3 failed | 15 passed`: DELETE by member, DELETE with no member (the reverse), and the cluster member reset were red, while stage 1's store-level reset pin stayed green. Restored: `18 passed`.
4. **The package-batch doors without the member.**
   - With the publish promotion's member dropped, the batch answered `success: false`, `outcome: refused`, `failed: [{ code: NO_DRAFT, error: No pending draft exists for email_template/acme.welcome — nothing to publish. }]`. That is the measured shape behind the changeset's sentence; both the publish and the revert pins were red.
   - With the discard's member dropped, the discard answered success while the `zh-CN` draft row stayed.
   - Both were restored, and the dist was proven absent.

These four ablations ran at `fdf01eb9e9`, the head before `2b882e6774` (the versioned harness package, the unshipped-member pin and the bundle-level shadow test), when the restart harness had 18 cases. The code each one removed is unchanged since. At `2b882e6774` the harness has 19 cases, all green.

## Deviations, stated

- **The value refusal's envelope.**
  - The selector's value is judged by the protocol, so the REST door renders that refusal through its one error door, `handleRouteError`. It comes out flat: `body.code` is `VALIDATION_ERROR`, and `body.error` is the sentence.
  - The route's own recognition refusal of a misspelled name is nested: `body.error.code`.
  - This is the existing split for every refusal the protocol raises on these routes (`check:route-envelope`, the repo-wide ratchet). The GET handler's own note says why converting part of it here would mint a new divergence.
  - The code is the same in both: `VALIDATION_ERROR`.
  - The `?layers=` plus `?member=` refusal is raised by the GET handler itself, not by the protocol. It is thrown into the same `handleRouteError`, so it is flat too; that is the handler's only pre-existing shape for a 400 of its own, so it mints no new dialect.
- **Response contracts are unchanged.**
  - `GET /meta/_drafts` and `GET /packages/:id/commits` do not serve `member`. The ruling widens the doors' accept set, not these responses.
  - Two drafts or plan items of one name in two languages therefore read as two entries with the same `type` and `name` there.
- **`removeRuntimeShadow` semantics, named member.** The artifact test stays at the level of the name: a packaged artifact of the bundle remains, as the method's contract always said, so it does not have to be an artifact of that member. Section 4 says why.
- **File surface.** Every edit is inside the claim's listed files, plus:
  - the four test files and the dogfood case the claim names;
  - `protocol.lookup-artifact-item-call-sites.test.ts`, whose census records the re-scoped artifact-lookup site and the definition's new parameter;
  - two regenerated artifacts: `authorable-surface/api.json` and the protocol reference page.

## Acceptance notes

- **The runtime dispatcher's `/meta` item read** (`packages/runtime/src/domains/meta.ts`) does not read `?member=`. A host served by the dispatcher alone would answer `GET …?member=zh-CN` with the canonical member, because that transport has no closed query set at all. The showcase is served by `RestServer` (measured by the dogfood case above). This is outside the claim's surface (`packages/runtime`), and is not measured on a dispatcher-only host.
- **By-name doors not in the ruling's list** stay canonical-only: `/diff`, `/layers`, `/audit`, `/published` and `/references`.
- **The MetadataService** (`MetadataManager`) keys a type's items by name alone, so for a bundle it holds one member. `getMetaItem` now takes its answer only when it is the addressed member; the service itself is unchanged.
- **The environment kernel's write-through.** On an environment kernel, a save and a peer's convergence do not write a non-object overlay through to the registry (#6602, by design). The cluster pin therefore boots control-plane replicas.
- **The untranslated `bundle_member` keys** stay owed to `area:i18n`, as the claim says.
